scenes.title: Pipes, Redirection & Chaining
scenes.narration: The real power of the shell appears when you connect small commands together into a single, expressive pipeline.

scenes.title: The Building Blocks
bullets: The pipe | sends the output of one command straight into the next.
The > operator redirects output into a file, overwriting whatever was there.
The >> operator appends output to the end of a file instead of replacing it.
The < operator feeds a file in as input to a command.
scenes.narration: Four small symbols unlock most of the shell's composability. The pipe passes one command's output into another as input, letting you build chains. A single greater-than sign redirects output into a file, wiping its previous contents, while the doubled form appends instead. And the less-than sign flows a file into a command as its input. Together these let data stream through many tools in one line.

scenes.title: How a Pipeline Flows
scenes.narration: Read a pipeline left to right, imagining data flowing through each stage. Here the log is emitted, filtered down to 404 errors, sorted so identical lines sit together, and finally counted by uniq. Each tool does one job, and the pipe stitches them into something greater.

scenes.title: Pipes in Action
scenes.code:
# how many ERROR lines are in the log?
grep "ERROR" app.log | wc -l

# save the errors to a file
grep "ERROR" app.log > errors.txt

# add today's errors to a running file
grep "ERROR" app.log >> all_errors.txt
scenes.narration: In the first example grep finds every error line and pipes it to wc -l, which counts them. The second example redirects those same lines into a fresh file with a single arrow. The third uses the double arrow so today's errors are appended to a growing history rather than clobbering it.

scenes.text: Small commands plus pipes equal big power — chain simple tools instead of hunting for one command that does everything.
scenes.narration: The Unix philosophy is to compose small, focused tools. Reach for a pipeline of simple commands rather than searching for a single monolithic one.
